Pain Management Consultation
Date: 09/05/2026
Patient: Adrian Wintheiser, 89-year-old male

Subjective:
Adrian Wintheiser presents with complaints of persistent right-sided lumbar pain radiating down the leg. Symptoms began on 04/06/2026, 22 weeks before this visit. Pain limits walking to about one block and has forced the patient to stop volunteering; sleep is disrupted most nights.

Objective:
Physical examination reveals decreased sensation in the right L4 dermatome and diminished strength in the right quadriceps muscle. Reflexes are reduced at the right patellar tendon. No signs of systemic illness.

Assessment:
Assessment: right lumbar radiculopathy at L4-L5 due to disc herniation with foraminal stenosis.

Plan:
Baseline NRS prior to any intervention: 7/10. Epidural steroid injection history: 2 lumbar injections in the past 12 months (03/05/2026, 05/14/2026). Continues the daily home exercise program taught in PT. Recommend continuation of conservative management with physical therapy and consideration of repeat epidural steroid injection if symptoms persist or worsen. Follow-up in 6 weeks to reassess pain and function.
